messages.subject: R1019 64-cell QSA decision report complete
messages.body: Audited the pinned QSA source geometry, declared local-memory arithmetic, BF16 online-softmax behavior, safety gates, and relevant Intel/SGLang/vLLM primary sources. The 64-cell tile is a bounded opt-in experiment candidate, not an adoption recommendation: it can cut long-tile barrier/loop count but doubles declared SLM to 47,936 B/WG, doubles serial softmax width, and changes BF16 probability rounding. Main must measure the isolated same-query 32-vs-64 path and validate framework numerical and physical-context gates; report: bench/results/2026-10-15-pr6-recovery-audit/research-round1019-v1.txt.

messages.subject: Layer-major upload overlap review complete
messages.body: I audited layer-major upload/drain ordering, source implementations, resolver paths, and existing staging/thread ownership, then wrote the bounded decision-support report. Main-thread copy-ahead into the drained slab after run_impl and before the checked pass drain is source-safe without another slab or math change, but available GPU overlap is unmeasured; worker and direct-DMA variants need extra source lifetime/thread-safety capabilities and have unresolved RAM constraints. The report gives required bounds, lifetime, cancellation, failure, and state invariants plus two falsifiable Main gates; no runtime tests or product edits were performed.
